By the matrix-tree theorem, the Laplacian eigenvalues of  
\(\Gamma=C_{11}\square C_{11}\) are

\[
\lambda_{a,b}=4-2\cos\frac{2\pi a}{11}-2\cos\frac{2\pi b}{11},
\qquad a,b\in \mathbb Z/11\mathbb Z.
\]

Thus

\[
\tau(\Gamma)=\frac1{121}\prod_{(a,b)\ne(0,0)}\lambda_{a,b}.
\]

Let

\[
x_k=2-2\cos\frac{2\pi k}{11}.
\]

Then \(\lambda_{a,b}=x_a+x_b\), with \(x_0=0\). Also

\[
\prod_{k=1}^{10}x_k=11^2,
\]

the usual product of the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues of \(C_{11}\). Therefore

\[
\tau(\Gamma)
=\frac1{121}\left(\prod_{a=1}^{10}x_a\right)^2
\prod_{a,b=1}^{10}(x_a+x_b)
=11^2\prod_{a,b=1}^{10}(x_a+x_b).
\]

Since \(x_k=x_{11-k}\), write \(r_1,\dots,r_5\) for the five distinct values. Then

\[
\prod_{a,b=1}^{10}(x_a+x_b)
=
\left(\prod_{i,j=1}^5(r_i+r_j)\right)^4.
\]

The numbers \(r_i\) are the roots of

\[
p(t)=t^5-11t^4+44t^3-77t^2+55t-11.
\]

A resultant computation gives

\[
\prod_{i,j=1}^5(r_i+r_j)
=\operatorname{Res}\bigl(p(t),-p(-t)\bigr)
=2^5\cdot 11^5\cdot 89^2\cdot 109^2.
\]

Hence

\[
\tau(\Gamma)
=11^2\left(2^5\cdot 11^5\cdot 89^2\cdot 109^2\right)^4.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{20}\cdot 11^{22}\cdot 89^8\cdot 109^8}
\]
